meta.title: Qwen Staged Repair — Resolved Design
meta.description: Failure-remediation ladder + staged repair lane: verdicts, routing, lanes, models, gates, and the full interview-loop resolution

props.title: Qwen Staged Repair
props.subtitle: Turn-level failure remediation, resolved: deterministic where the parse already knows, model-planned only where it doesn't, everything in shadow until it proves itself.

props.content: One CDO deliberation (8 agents, adversarial verify) killed the unsafe half of the ladder concept; a 9-turn interview loop then specified every surviving branch down to file paths, schemas, and gates. The design artifact is .lev/pm/designs/20260703-qwen-staged-repair-loop.md — this page is its readable projection.

props.label: CDO DELIBERATION
props.title: The four ladder elements — what survived
props.subtitle: 2-turn, 8-agent deliberation with a devil's-advocate pass that materially corrected Turn 1

rows.why: Authority grounds only: recovery's own contract emits ask_say_again — a competing say-again authority. The latency objection was retracted (measured p50 ≈ 3.0 s, already awaited inline today). Recovery demoted to background advisor.

rows.element: Background repair agent in the say-again window
rows.why: Candidate-only through PolicyChain shadow, never auto-releases. Sync shadow lane measured first; async apparatus is the last slice, gated on Gate β.

Rehabilitated as instrument: for no_intent failures there are no slots to compare — fuzzy text is the only always-present signal (echo.py precedent, 100% TP at 0 FP). But demoted to cancellation/correlation; never a release decision.
Unreachable by the trigger predicates regardless of calibration: a ≥0.99 fresh parse never enters the ladder; a ≥0.99 pre-parse contradicts the trigger.

props.title: Binding collapse rule (elements 3+4)
props.content: Always fresh-parse the post-say-again re-transmission. Repair-agent output enters as one more PolicyChain candidate into THAT fresh parse. Repair work is a hint — never the source of truth. This one rule deletes the stale-answer and double-transmission races by construction.

props.label: S1
props.title: Failure-class routing
props.subtitle: The Turn-1 discovery that reshaped everything: 5 of 6 failure classes are mechanically derivable — the model only earns its keep on no_intent

rows.evidence: intent + exact missing slot names + contract_row_id
full intent + params + validation (dormant: regex emits 1.0/0.0)

rows.derivation: Data defect — file to template authoring, no model budget
The one class with no structured evidence — deterministic classifier control vs stage-1 planner

props.label: S3 / S4 / S7
props.title: Four lanes, one contract
props.subtitle: All shadow, all through the same executor and EvidencePack, separately named for per-lane would-have-won attribution

props.title: ⚙️ deterministic_repair_derivation — tier 58
props.content: No model call for planning. Query key derived mechanically from raw.validation. Covers 4 failure classes and serves as the control on no_intent via the generated-template classifier. Ships first — proves executor, pack, and parity before any model lane.

props.title: 🅰️ qwen_staged_repair_a — tier 62
props.content: Caller-mediated query plan. New POST /plan on the parser sidecar returns classification + QueryPlan in one call; the pipeline executes retrieval; Stage 2 parses with the pack. Fail-closed: any malformed plan drops whole → provider_failed. Output enforcement: strict-parse-reject (Outlines constrained decoding = open 🔑 dependency decision).

props.title: 🅱️ qwen_staged_repair_b — tier 64
props.content: Pipeline-driven tool loop. The pipeline stays the chat client: sidecar emits tool calls, pipeline executes the SAME executor, appends canonical-JSON results, re-POSTs until final parse or max_turns. Honest framing: caller-mediated with extra steps — the only delta is adaptive per-query authoring. Kill rule: if it never beats the one-shot plan, delete it.

props.title: 📊 qwen_structured_parse — tier 60 (existing)
props.content: The plain-parse control: today's evidence-free qwen candidate source, unchanged. Every model lane must beat both this AND the deterministic control to justify its existence.

props.label: TOPOLOGY
props.title: One repaired turn, end to end

props.content:
flowchart TD
    T[repair_trigger fires\nsegment_candidate_arbitration] --> R{failure_class\nrouting policy}
    R -->|parser_contract_invalid| AUTH[File to template authoring\nno repair]
    R -->|4 mechanical classes| DET[Deterministic lane\nquery = intent + offending slots]
    R -->|no_intent| ALL[All three lanes in shadow]
    ALL --> CTRL[Deterministic control\ngenerated_template classifier]
    ALL --> VA[Variant a\nPOST /plan → QueryPlan]
    ALL --> VB[Variant b\npipeline-driven tool loop]
    DET --> EX[EvidenceQueryExecutor\n3 query kinds, deterministic order]
    CTRL --> EX
    VA --> EX
    VB -.per tool call.-> EX
    EX --> PACK[EvidencePack\ncanonical JSON, digests, ≤4KB]
    PACK --> S2[Stage 2: /parse + evidence\nV27a adapter re-prompted]
    S2 --> IV[provider_ingress_validation]
    IV --> PC[PolicyChain — mode: shadow\ncannot win, per-lane attribution]
    PC --> TR[REPAIR_TRACE_EVENT per turn+lane\naudit JSONL + baseline repair_ladder]

props.label: S2
props.title: Evidence contract and pack
props.subtitle: Three query kinds; the raw 1.8 KB template row becomes a 150 B projection

props.content:
**Three query kinds** cover everything: `template_rows_by_intent` (new by-intent index on the templates authority), `slot_constraints_for_intent` (existing bounds map + parameter roles), and `intent_family_candidates` (existing classifier — the only kind the planner adds).

Determinism is provable, not asserted: every query result carries a `result_digest`, the pack carries a `data_version` (sha256 over the authority files read), truncation drops whole tail rows after a deterministic sort, and the parity gate compares digests byte-for-byte.

Ownership stays clean: contract types and executor live in the new `modules/intent/evidence_query/` leaf as read-models; `modules/authority` remains the sole data owner; budgets and routing live in the `staged_repair:` policy block — no Python literals.

class EvidencePack(BaseModel):
    schema_version: str
    data_version: str            # sha256 over authority files read
    failure_class: FailureClass
    intent: str | None
    offending_slots: list[str]
    template_rows: list[TemplateRowProjection]   # ~150 B each, max 8
    slot_constraints: list[SlotConstraint]
    intent_family_candidates: list[FamilyCandidate]
    queries_executed: list[ExecutedQueryRecord]  # each with result_digest
    truncated: bool

# TemplateRowProjection keeps: row_id, intent, atc_phrase_text,
# slots, required_slots, slot_key_space
# DROPS: source, docling, faa_page_path, pilot_readback (1.8KB -> 150B)

props.label: S5
props.title: Model selection
props.subtitle: Deep research (mid-2026 landscape) + repo verification: no new model needed

rows.notes: Confirmed same base as V27a; prior art already loads it bare (poc/atc_recovery_planner). Outlines schema enforcement = 🔑 open dep decision
Native Hermes-style tool template; loop runs in-process batch-of-1 — never via mlx_lm.server's unmerged tool plumbing
Pack is RAG-style in-context evidence (matches queued rag_fewshot_top1 lever). Retrain only if the pack shifts distribution
2026 tool-calling leader, but MLX conversion gaps + merged-LoRA greedy-divergence bug + thinking-mode default

props.title: Determinism finding from research
props.content: Temperature-0 is NOT deterministic under concurrent batching (1000 temp-0 runs → 80 unique completions in one study). The repo's in-process, batch-of-1, mlx-lm greedy pattern IS run-to-run reproducible on a pinned version — which is exactly why the tool loop is pipeline-driven and batch-of-1.

props.label: S8
props.title: Measurement — extend, never fork
props.subtitle: Hooks the existing recovery-scorer line in tooling/baseline/runner.py; binary gold-match scorer reused; all fields additive so zero scored-row movement stays provable

props.title: 🎯 repair_hit_rate[lane]
props.content: Gold-matching candidates ÷ ALL failing rows in the lane's routing scope. Anti-gaming rule: the denominator is routing scope, never rows-where-the-lane-fired — an abstain-happy planner cannot shrink its own denominator. Fired-count surfaced separately.

props.title: 🚫 false_accept[lane]
props.content: Structurally-selectable candidates that diverge from gold, counted over ALL scored rows including passing ones — corrupting a good row is the danger. Raw count; Gate α requires exactly zero.

props.title: 🔁 multi_turn_rate[lane]
props.content: Hits needing turns_used > 1 ÷ all hits, plus the turns histogram {1, 2, budget_exceeded}. Renamed from standby_rate — nothing here speaks on the radio. The 1-shot vs 2-shot Δ comes from a config-overlay A/B, not a baseline fork.

props.title: Gates and kill criteria
props.content: Gate α (fund the ledger work): no_intent model-lane hit-rate ≥ ~25%, beats the deterministic control, 2-shot beats 1-shot by ≥ ~10 pp, zero false accepts. Gate β (fund async): 2-shot doesn't fit inline but fits the say-again window with ≥2 s margin. Kill: hit-rate <10% · any false accept · control ties the planner (delete planner) · adaptive never beats one-shot (delete variant b) · parity unfixable. α/β numbers are placeholders — ratify in the workstream before Slice-3 measurement.

items.title: Model spikes + frozen fixtures (∥ Slice 1)
items.description: Two-handle serving (base + adapter in one process), bare-base plan-JSON quality, tool-template determinism, data-availability probe fixtures frozen, 🔑 Outlines decision. Bench deferred to pre-Gate-β.

items.title: evidence_query leaf
items.description: Contract types, deterministic executor, StagedRepairDriver, probe + unit tests, Null/Static providers. Pure new code — zero collision risk.

items.title: Shadow lanes through PolicyChain (⚠ option-A)
items.description: Three policy blocks, /plan + agentic endpoints, prompt registry. Gate: leakage regression green, parity green, zero scored-row movement.

items.title: Baseline metric extension
items.description: apply_repair_ladder_scores + repair_ladder rollup + display block. Gate: parity green twice. GATE α decides everything after this.

items.title: RepairLedger + say-again gold pack (post-α)
items.description: Turn lineage, fuzzy-text correlation/cancellation, correlation-key design (no chain_id links consecutive ATC turns today), divergence policy on a readback/authority surface; 10–20 hand-authored say-again exchanges.

items.title: Async apparatus (conditional on GATE β)
items.description: Keyed task ledger, cancel-on-divergence, at-most-once epoch-checked release. Gate: W1–W7 race tests, at-most-once property test, parity, periodic final-boss.

props.label: WHAT'S LEFT
props.title: Open decisions and immediate next moves
🔑 Outlines dependency
props.content: JSON-schema constrained decoding over mlx-lm: ~20-line change, eliminates the invalid-JSON abstain class for both planner lanes, guarantees plan shape. But it is a new dependency — needs explicit approval before Slice 0 closes.

props.title: 🔑 Ratify Gate α/β numbers
props.content: The ~25% hit-rate, ~10 pp 2-shot delta, and ~2 s window margin are design-judgment placeholders. Write the final numbers into the workstream BEFORE the Slice-3 measurement run so the gate can't be negotiated after seeing the data.

props.title: ✅ Shovel-ready
props.content: Slices 0 and 1 are fully specified and parallel: model spikes + frozen fixtures, and the evidence_query leaf with its test matrix. /propose can compile them into an execution packet directly from the design's Design-to-Propose Handoff section.
